summary: This RFC is the formal specification of the Exterior Gateway Protocol, used between gateways of different autonomous systems in the ARPA Internet. It updates parts of RFC 888 and RFC 827. It is historic as a protocol now.

eli5.summary: Neighboring networks needed a way to tell each other which addresses they can reach. EGP was an early way to share that routing news.

questions: what is the exterior gateway protocol
how did egp exchange routes between autonomous systems
what is egp hello and i-h-u
subtitle: The formal state machine and message formats gateways used to tell each other which networks they could reach.

tldr.problem: Gateways in different autonomous systems of the ARPA Internet needed a precise, implementable way to find each other, check each other is alive and exchange net-reachability information.
tldr.mechanism: EGP defines a five-state machine per neighbor. Gateways acquire a neighbor with Request/Confirm, monitor it with Hello and I-H-U messages, and fetch reachability with Poll and Update messages.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is marked Historic. It was a reference for implementation and testing, and its own text expected it to be amended or obsoleted as EGP grew to full routing.

today: RFC 904 is marked Historic, so EGP is no longer a current protocol. It updated RFC 827 and RFC 888, and this site's records list no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: What EGP Is For
sections.content:
The Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP) exchanges net-reachability information between Internet gateways that belong to the same or different autonomous systems. This RFC is a formal specification meant as a reference for implementation, testing and verification, with suggested algorithm parameters. It states that interactions between gateways of different autonomous systems in the ARPA-Internet must follow this protocol, and it updates RFC 827 and RFC 888.

Background, application and limitations of EGP are deliberately left to those earlier RFCs. The RFC expects that if EGP grows to include topologies beyond trees and full routing capabilities, this specification will be amended or obsoleted, while the basic mechanisms stay the same and only the format and meaning of the Update message change.

The protocol is based on periodic polling. Hello and I-Heard-You (I-H-U) exchanges monitor neighbor reachability, and Poll commands ask for Update responses that carry the reachability data. All gateways must also support ICMP Redirect and Destination Unreachable messages.
sections.eli5: Two neighbors say hello now and then to check the other is still there, and ask now and then for an updated list of reachable places.

sections.title: The Neighbor State Machine
sections.content:
Each gateway keeps a separate state machine, with its own variables, for every neighbor. There are five states: Idle (0), Acquisition (1), Down (2), Up (3) and Cease (4). In Idle, no resources are assigned to the neighbor. A Start event sends a Request and moves to Acquisition, where Request is retransmitted until the neighbor answers with Confirm (go to Down) or Refuse (back to Idle). Receiving a Request in Idle gives a Confirm and a move to Down, or a Refuse if resources do not permit.

In Down, the neighbor is considered unreachable, and Hello commands are sent if enabled. When the reachability algorithm declares the neighbor up, the machine moves to Up and starts sending Poll commands as well. A Stop event, from the operator or the abort timer, sends a Cease command and enters Cease, which retransmits until a Cease-ack arrives. A received Cease always gets a Cease-ack and a return to Idle.

Messages are classed as commands (Request, Cease, Hello, Poll), responses (Confirm, Refuse, Cease-ack, I-H-U, Update, Error) and indications, which may be sent at any time. Implementations may deviate from the model while conforming, but the model is the reference for verifying conformance.
sections.eli5: The two gateways go through steps: not talking, asking to be friends, friends who are not sure the other is awake, friends who are sure, and finally saying goodbye politely.

sections.title: Reachability and Timers
sections.content:
Neighbor reachability is judged with a sliding window. In active mode a gateway sends Hello commands and counts I-H-U responses. In passive mode it counts the Status field in received Hello or Poll commands. At least one neighbor must be active. The Up event fires when at least j indications arrive within T3 seconds, and Down when at most k do. Suggested values are j=3, k=1 for active and j=1, k=4 for passive, with T3 suggested as four times T1. This filters noise so that the wider Internet is not hit by needless reachability changes.

Suggested fixed parameters include P1 of 30 seconds (minimum acceptable interval between Hello commands), P2 of 2 minutes (between Polls), P3 of 30 seconds (between Request or Cease retransmissions), P4 of 1 hour and P5 of 2 minutes for the optional abort timer. Polling intervals are negotiated in the Request/Confirm exchange.

Network reachability travels in Update messages as lists of gateways on a common network, each with the networks reachable through it and a hop count. An internal list covers gateways in the sender's own autonomous system, and an external list covers gateways in others. Hop counts are not a routing metric and are comparable only inside one system. Only gateways in the designated core system may include the external list. Error messages are advisory and never sent in response to another Error.
sections.eli5: Not one missed hello means the friend is gone. The gateway counts how many hellos it heard recently, and only changes its mind when enough pile up one way.

sections.title: Message Formats
sections.content:
Every EGP message starts with a ten-octet header made up of EGP Version (currently 2), Type, Code, Status, Checksum, Autonomous System number and Sequence number. The checksum is the 16-bit one's complement of the one's complement sum of the message. The sequence number is the send variable for commands and the receive variable for responses and indications.

The message types are: Type 3 for neighbor acquisition (Code 0 Request, 1 Confirm, 2 Refuse, 3 Cease, 4 Cease-ack), Type 5 for neighbor reachability (Code 0 Hello, 1 I-H-U) and Type 2 for Poll. Request and Confirm add Hello Interval and Poll Interval fields. Acquisition Status values include 1 active mode, 2 passive mode, 3 insufficient resources, 4 administratively prohibited, 5 going down, 6 parameter problem and 7 protocol violation. The Update response lists internal and external gateways with distances and nets.
sections.eli5: Every message starts with the same small label saying who it is from, what kind of message it is and its number in the conversation.

fields.name: EGP Version
fields.desc: Assigned number identifying the EGP version (currently 2).

fields.name: Checksum
fields.desc: 16-bit one's complement of the one's complement sum of the message.

fields.name: Autonomous System #
fields.desc: Assigned number identifying the autonomous system.

fields.name: Sequence #
fields.desc: Send variable for commands, receive variable for responses and indications.
